script.title: Private vs Public Company
script.caption_hook: Private or public company? Same Act, very different rules!

lines.say: Both are companies under one Act. So what's actually different?
A private company is closed: restricted share transfer, at most 200 members, no inviting the public. A public company is open.
How do I tell them apart?
Private: shares can't move freely, and no public invitation. Public: shares transfer freely, and it may invite the public.
And members? Is there a limit?
Private: minimum 2 members, maximum 200, excluding present and certain former employee-members. Public: minimum 7, no maximum.
No, joint holders count as one. And a One Person Company, a private company, can have one member.
Private needs 2 directors, OPC needs 1. Public needs 3. Memory trick: private two-two, public seven-three.
Wait, what if a private company is a public company's subsidiary?
It's deemed public under the Act, even if its articles keep private restrictions.
Oh! So private is closed, public is open.
Private is closed, public is open. Remember two-two, seven-three.

Checker: Line 10 board (versus): the figures '2 members', '2 directors', '7 members', '3 directors' should be labelled as minimums, e.g. 'Min 2 members', 'Min 2 directors' / 'Min 7 members', 'Min 3 directors'. Public directors can go up to 15 under s.149(1) without a special resolution. The voice line 'Private needs 2 directors' should also say 'at least 2 directors'.

Checker: Line 8: 'a One Person Company ... can have one member' understates the rule. A One Person Company has only one member (s.2(62)). Better: 'a One Person Company, a type of private company, has only one member.'
